core: Causal determinism as a thesis about states of the world and laws of nature
Why the thesis differs from a local causal explanation
The distinction between determinism, predictability, and fatalism
The conditional relevance of determinism to free-will debates

claims.claim: Causal determinism is roughly the thesis that a specified state of the world at a time together with laws of nature fixes the way things go afterward.
The determinist thesis is stronger than the observation that particular earlier factors influence later events, because it concerns the relation of a complete state and laws to a unique future.

Determinism and predictability are logically distinct: a system may be deterministic while finite observers lack information or computational ability to predict it, and some predictable behavior need not establish global determinism.
Fatalism is distinguishable from determinism because fatalism says events occur regardless of what agents do, whereas determinism concerns dependence on states and natural laws.
Whether the actual world is deterministic is a contingent and contested issue; philosophical clarification does not by itself settle the status of physical theories.

Determinism provides a premise in debates about free will, but it does not by itself settle whether an agent is free or morally responsible because those conclusions require further accounts of agency and responsibility.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether the actual world is deterministic and what scientific theories imply about that question.
positions: Some physical theories and interpretations have been treated as deterministic or as support for determinism.
Other theories or interpretations are treated as probabilistic or indeterministic, and philosophers disagree about what follows.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson does not announce a scientific verdict. It explains the thesis and states that its truth remains contested.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether determinism eliminates free will or moral responsibility.
positions: Incompatibilist arguments treat a fixed past and laws as a challenge to relevant freedom.
Compatibilist accounts argue that some forms of freedom can coexist with causal determinism.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson identifies this as a downstream debate and refers readers to Free Will rather than defending either account.
